text: [curious] And the first result looks like a contradiction. Leah's variable rate rose above nine percent at some point in seventy-six point two percent of stretches, about three in four. Yet it cost more in total interest in fourteen point two percent, about one in seven. That one in seven is made of two very different parts: twenty-eight point four percent, more than one in four, for starts from nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty, and three point five percent, about one in thirty, from nineteen eighty-one on; the worst stretch, from April nineteen seventy-seven, cost eleven thousand two hundred nineteen dollars more. The reason both are true is the head start.
